title: Serial Versus Parallel Cost Calculator
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: AI Agents
Token Budgets
Parallel Execution
Cost Estimation
description: Three sliders set the number of sub-tasks, the tokens of real work per sub-task, and the startup overhead per agent. Two stacked bars compare the serial total (overhead paid once) with the parallel total (overhead paid once per agent), and a verdict line reports how many more tokens parallel execution costs.

educational.topic: Token cost of serial versus parallel agent execution
learningObjectives: Calculate the total token cost of a task run serially versus in parallel.
Identify the agent-count threshold where parallel execution stops paying off.
prerequisites: Knows what a token is and that plans limit token use
Has read the definitions of sub-agent startup overhead, serial agent execution, and parallel agent execution

controls.label: Tokens of real work per sub-task
Show formula
controls.description: Reveals the serial and parallel totals as live-updating equations

equations: serial total = (work tokens x sub-tasks) + (1 x startup overhead)
parallel total = (work tokens x sub-tasks) + (sub-tasks x startup overhead)
assumptions: Every sub-task needs the same number of work tokens
Parallel execution uses exactly one agent per sub-task
The verdict reads 'about the same' when parallel costs less than 5% more than serial
limitations: Counts tokens only; elapsed time, rate limits, failed agents, and context reuse are not modeled
The default overhead of 12,000 tokens is a rough figure from this book's own project

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: The learner plugs in values and reads the recomputed totals instead of trusting a quoted percentage
keyQuestions: Which slider changes the number of extra tokens, and which changes only the percentage?
At what number of agents does the extra cost exceed your own tolerance?
commonMisconceptions: Parallel execution costs the same tokens and is simply faster
The extra cost of parallel execution depends on how much real work there is
assessmentOpportunities: Given a tolerance for extra cost, find the largest number of sub-tasks that stays within it
